info.title: Content Transformation Studio API
info.description:
Content Transformation Studio (CT Studio) extracts the contents of PDFs whose structure is known
in advance and publishes them as validated CSV and JSON. This API is what the web app uses.

## Signing in

Every `/api` route needs a session except `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`
and these docs. Sign in with your email address and password; the response sets the
`ih_session` cookie, which the browser sends with every request. Signed out, a guarded route
answers `401` `{ "error": "sign in required" }`. A session opened with a one-time password
can only read `GET /api/auth/me` and change the password (`PUT /api/auth/password`); every
other guarded route answers `403` `{ "error": "change your one-time password first" }`.
"Try it" in these docs uses your session when you are signed in to the app in the same
browser.

A request that changes something (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) and that the
browser marks as sent from another site's page (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`) is refused
with `403` `{ "error": "cross-site request refused" }`, signing in included. Scripts and
other clients that send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` are unaffected.

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "message" }`, or `{ "error": [ ...Zod issues ] }` for some
validation failures. IDs are UUIDs; a malformed ID is a `404`, the same as an unknown one.

## Admin routes

Routes marked **Admins only** (`x-admin: true`) answer `403`
`{ "error": "admins only" }` to a user who is not an admin.

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and a password
post.description:
Opens a session and sets the `ih_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure
when the request came over HTTPS). A session ends 30 days after sign-in, or after 7
days without use. `login` is the email address, or `admin` for the admin from the
API log, whose password is the token the API prints on every start.

A session opened with a one-time password (`mustChangePassword: true`) can only read
`/api/auth/me`, change the password and sign out until the password is changed.

An unknown email and a wrong password are the same `401`. The 10th
failed sign-in in a row locks the account for 15 minutes, each one after doubles the
lock (at most 24 hours), and the 20th disables the account until an
admin enables it; the admin from the log is never locked. While locked, any password
gets `429` with `lockedUntil`, unchecked. Separately, after 10 failed attempts in 15
minutes a client (an IP address, or an IPv6 /64) gets `429` until older failures
age out. Every attempt is recorded for admins (`GET /api/sign-ins`).

put.description:
Changes the signed-in user's password; with a one-time password session this is the
first sign-in step. The new password is 12 to 200 characters, differs from the current
one and does not contain the email address. Every other session of the user ends;
this one stays signed in.

A wrong current password counts as a failed sign-in and can lock the account, as for
sign-in. The admin from the API log cannot change its password: it rotates on every
API start.

newPassword.description: 12 to 200 characters, different from the current one, not containing the email address.

one Connect issued to this browser in the last 10 minutes, and
it works once. Redirects to the app's Profile dialog with `github=` `linked`,
`denied` (you said no on GitHub), `expired` (the state is unknown, used or not

post.summary: Import a recipe version from GitHub as a new document type
post.description:
Reads the file at `path` (`<root>/<instance>/<type-id>/v<N>.yaml`) at `commit`
with **your** linked GitHub account and creates a new document type from it: a v1
**draft**, never published. `id` defaults to the file's type id and `name` to the
definition's name. The file's label and note are copied. An id that exists already is
a 409 (pull into it from its Versions tab, or import under another id), and so is a
retired one. With `link: true` an admin also links the new type to the repository
(this repo, branch and root; it pushes each published version, without pull
requests); for anyone else the type is created and `linked` is false.

post.summary: Upload a PDF or Word document to process
post.description:
Stores the file in the inbox bucket, records the document and queues a `process`
job for it. The worker picks the job up; poll `GET /api/jobs/{id}` for its status.
A Word document (`.docx`) is converted to PDF by the worker first, and then
processed like a PDF (pages come from the converted PDF).

Send the text fields **before** the file part: the upload is read as it streams in, so
fields after the file are not seen.

- `specId` names the document type; `specVersion` picks a version (default: the
  latest published one, or the newest spec file).
- A draft recipe version can only be uploaded as a test run (`test=true`). Test
  runs can be reviewed but are never delivered to the target.
- `model` overrides the document type's model for every step: a model choice's id
  from `GET /api/models/choices` (`default` is the default choice), or an
  offered `endpoint/model` ref from `GET /api/models`.
- A retired document type is refused (409) until an admin unretires it.

The file's bytes decide what it is, never its name: a PDF (starting `%PDF-`) or a
`.docx` (a Word document; not `.docm`, `.dotx` or `.doc`) without tracked
changes. It must fit the upload limit (`MAX_UPLOAD_MB`). The job's
`contentType` says which it is.

model.description: A model choice's id (or an offered model ref) to use instead of the document type's models.

post.description:
Bulk version of `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}` for finished jobs last updated before a
cutoff (now minus `olderThanDays`). Regression runs are kept unless
`includeRegression` is true, since scores and metrics are computed from them.
Like a single delete, it **withdraws what the jobs delivered**: their published
outputs leave the final target (the data lake) and their graphs the triple store.

`cutoff`. Then delete with `dryRun: false`, passing that `cutoff` so the
delete matches what was previewed. Each request deletes at most `limit` jobs and
reports how many are `remaining`; repeat while it is above 0. A job whose status
changed in between is skipped.

post.summary: Re-run one extract or plugin step
post.description:
Queues one extract or plugin step of a job awaiting review again, optionally with
another model, extra instructions, or pages sent as images so a vision model reads
them directly (e.g. handwriting). The worker reuses the document's text and OCR and
re-runs the checks; the job returns to `awaiting_review` with the step's new values.

A plugin step takes `instructions` (the plugin reads them as `ctx.instructions`),
a `model` only when its plugin asks one (egress `model` in `GET /api/plugins`),
and no `pageImages`.

Refused while the step's outputs have reviewer edits, since a re-run would discard
them: for a step enriching a table, edits of its own columns; for the step creating a
table's rows, any edit of the table, since its enriching steps re-run with it. `model` must be offered (`GET /api/models`) or an alias resolving to one.

`ids` names them; each row's `retired` is read live.

get.description:
Whether the open draft meets the holdout bar. Informational only: references and
evaluation are optional, and publishing never needs the gate. The newest complete
holdout iteration that evaluated the draft exactly as it is now (version and
definition), with the recipe's own models, decides. It passes only when it covered
every ready holdout sample, compared every sample it evaluated (a job that failed,
needs review, was cancelled or deleted fails it), and scored at or above the
project's threshold. `reason` says why it passes or fails. Scores are recomputed
from the models' raw output, so review edits cannot raise them.

`hints` (handoff EV1) are the deciding iteration's fields and `table.column`s
below the threshold, worst first, at most 5: `no_step` when no step of the draft
fills the output (fix on the Pipeline tab, `stage: steps`), else `low_accuracy`
(`stage: revise`). Empty without a deciding iteration. The overview's `gate`
carries no hints.

Publishes the open draft when it is valid. References and evaluation are optional: the
publish gate is informational only, and its iteration and score (if any) are recorded
with the publication. `overrideReason` is still accepted but ignored (no override is
needed or recorded). `label` and `note`, when given, are set on the version
(#144; it keeps the draft's otherwise). If the draft changes after the gate was decided, nothing is published: check the gate
again. Every publication is logged (`GET …/publications`). The Templates route
(`POST /api/templates/{id}/versions/{version}/publish`) publishes a Workbench
document type the same way. See
[ADR 0007](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-workbench.md).

post.description:
Asks the drafting model (the `draft` alias) for a stage's proposal, as a `draft`
job; poll `GET …/proposals`. Stages run in order (`survey`, `outputs`,
`sections`, `steps`): an earlier stage must be accepted or skipped first.

- `survey` proposes questions about the document type; the other stages propose
  typed changes to the open draft (fields and tables, sections and copies, steps).
  The `sections` stage checks its anchors on every dev sample and gets one round of
  feedback.
- `revise` (outside the order, cannot be skipped) answers the open feedback and the
  latest dev evaluation's failures; it needs open feedback.
- `mapping` (ADR 0011; outside the order, optional) proposes the recipe's ontology
  mapping from the brief's vocabulary ontologies, using the values the dev samples'
  latest runs produced; it needs the outputs stage complete and ready ontology versions.
- `references` instead queues reference runs (`201` with the jobs): the draft
  model on every ready dev sample without a reference, stopped for review so the
  values can be verified and saved as references.

Only dev samples are ever sent to the model (the holdout rule). A `local` project
only uses local models.

post.description:
Clears `stale` from a stage without a new proposal (the Sections tab's _Keep these
anchors_): its current content is confirmed against the earlier stages as they are now.
Its `completedAt` and its state (`accepted`, or `skipped` for a kept skip) are
unchanged, so later stages do not go stale; an earlier stage completing again makes it
stale again. Only `outputs`, `sections` and `steps` can be kept, and only while
stale. Nothing is proposed and the draft is not changed.

post.description:
Decides a ready proposal. Rejecting, or accepting a survey, records the decision.
Accepting a change proposal applies the chosen `changes` (indexes into its list;
all of them for `accepted`, some for `partially_accepted`) to the open draft.
A proposal with no changes is accepted with `changes: []`: the draft is unchanged and
a stage that was already complete is kept (as by its `confirm`), not completed again.
It is refused when the draft version changed since the proposal, or when the draft
was edited where a chosen change applies (accept the others, or run the stage again).
Accepting a `revise` proposal, fully or partly, resolves the feedback its applied
changes answer (their `answers`); a proposal whose changes name none resolves all the
feedback it was sent.

post.summary: Evaluate the draft against the references
post.description:

that has a verified reference, one test job each, and records an iteration with a
snapshot of the definition. The scorecard fills in as the jobs finish (poll
`GET …/iterations/{iid}`).

`model` overrides every step with a model choice (its id from
`GET /api/models/choices`; `default` is the default choice) for exploration; an
unknown choice, or an external one for a local-only project, is a 400; only iterations with the recipe's own models count for the publish
gate. `uncached` makes every step call its model instead of reusing the step cache.
Holdout scores always compare the models' raw output, never reviewed values.

as one `file` part each, or of one `.zip` part (hidden entries and others are
left out), imported in one go, at most 300 files within the upload
limit. Fields come before the files:

- `mode`: `merge` makes the files one version of the ontology `id` (a new
  ontology needs `label`); imports between them are `included`. The same set of
  files twice is refused (409).
- `separate` makes each file the next version of the ontology
  `<idPrefix><file name>`, all imported by one job, so imports between them
  resolve to each other. A file already a version of its ontology is skipped.
- `paths`: a JSON array of the files' paths in the folder, in part order (browsers
  send only the file name).

The answer lists the versions queued and the files skipped.

label.description: `merge`: the name of a new ontology.

idPrefix.description: `separate`: prefix of every id, e.g. `idmp-` (may be empty).

tags.description: Comma-separated tags for new ontologies.

localOnly.description: `true`: never sent to external models (new ontologies).

paths.description: JSON array of the files' paths, in order.

file.description: An ontology file (repeat the part per file), or one .zip. Send them last.

post.summary: Name the terms of a mapping
post.description:
The readable name of each term a recipe's mapping uses, for the Mapping tab: send
the pinned versions, the recipe's prefixes and local terms, and the terms as
written (CURIEs or IRIs, at most 500). Each term is expanded as the
recipe check expands it, then named from its local term, else the first pinned
version (in the order sent, imports included) holding it. `from` says which:
`ontology`, `local`, `built-in` (rdf, rdfs, owl, xsd, skos, dcterms, prov;
no label), `unknown` (in none of them) or `invalid` (an undeclared prefix).
Each name comes with the term's synonyms (`altLabels`) and definition (a local
term's own, when it has one), so a reviewer can judge a mapping by what the term means.
Nothing is checked against readiness: a version that is not indexed names nothing.

class, and the KMS key is cleared whenever the encryption is not `aws:kms`. An
internal target cannot move onto CT Studio's own inbox, outputs, runs or backups
bucket (400). While the target is in use (a published recipe version names it, an
output or graph copy was delivered to it, an S3 key consumer is granted it, or a
withdrawal still to run names it) its bucket and prefix cannot change (409): add a
new target and publish a version naming it instead. The label, connection,
encryption and storage class may always change, so keys are rotated without a new
version. The change is mirrored to the bridge; when the bridge refuses it (422) or
cannot be reached (502), the target is left as it was.

post.summary: Check an uploaded backup before restoring it
post.description:
**Admins only.** Starts the check of a completed upload in the background: the whole
file is decrypted and verified, and nothing changes yet. `deployment` (disaster
recovery, a server move) opens it with this server's `LLM_SECRETS_KEY`, then
`LLM_SECRETS_KEY_PREVIOUS`; `copy` (production into staging) with `key`, the
`LLM_SECRETS_KEY` of the deployment it came from, used for this restore only and never
stored. A key that does not open the file ends the check as failed with
`this key does not open the backup`.

The answer carries `token`, shown once: keep it to follow the restore
(`GET /api/backup/restores/{id}`) and confirm it once `phase` is `checked`, since a
restore signs everyone out. From here until the restore ends or is cancelled, no
backup, upload or other restore can start. A checked restore not confirmed within 30
minutes is cancelled (`the check expired: start the restore again`): its key is not kept longer.

token.description: Send it as `X-Restore-Token`; it is not shown again.

(the UTC date, `N` from 1 each day), and the deploy bakes the tag into the images. A

tags.name: Documents
tags.description:
Upload a PDF to process it with a document type. The API stores the file in the inbox
bucket, records a document and queues a job; the worker does the rest.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description:
A job processes one document with one version of a document type. Jobs move through
`queued`, `running` and then `succeeded`, `awaiting_review`, `needs_review`
(a processing problem for an operator), `failed` (after retries), `rejected` or
`cancelled`. See the [job lifecycle](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#job-lifecycle).

tags.name: Review & steps
tags.description:
Jobs of document types with a review policy stop in `awaiting_review`. Reviewers read the
draft outputs, record edits, then approve (the edited outputs are published) or reject
(final). Each extraction step's run can be inspected and re-run.

tags.name: Results
tags.description:
Published outputs, read from the publishing target each was delivered to: the documents a job delivered, their
values and their files.

tags.name: Specs
tags.description:
Document types as uploads see them: database recipes and the definitions loaded from the
repository's `specs/` folder (legacy `spec.yaml` and `template.yaml`). Versions are
immutable once published. An admin can retire a document type (hidden from new work, still
readable; also on the Document types page) and unretire it (here only).

tags.name: Recipes
tags.description:
Transformation recipes: each document type's definition (outputs, sections, pipeline steps,
review policy, default model), kept in the database. Drafts are editable, published versions
are immutable. Recipes import and export as YAML. See
[ADR 0003](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-versioned-document-specs.md).

tags.name: References & regression
tags.description:
References are verified output values for a sample PDF. Regression runs process the
references' PDFs with a recipe version and score the outputs against them; metrics
summarise a document type's runs.

tags.name: Models
tags.description:
Language models the worker discovered from the configured providers. Model refs are
`provider/model-id` or an alias such as `default` or `fast`.

tags.name: Projects & data policy
tags.description:
The Workbench builds a document type from sample PDFs, one project per type (the project id
is the recipe id). A project's data policy decides whether its documents may be sent to
external model providers (`external`) or only to local ones (`local`). See
[ADR 0007](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-workbench.md) and the
[Workbench design](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/design/workbench.md).

tags.name: Samples & brief
tags.description:
Samples are the project's PDFs, each in the **dev** set (seen by drafting) or the
**holdout** set (used only to score). Uploading a sample prepares its text (with OCR where
needed). The brief describes what the document type must extract.

tags.name: Drafting stages & proposals
tags.description:
A drafting model proposes the recipe in stages (survey, outputs, sections, steps), each a
set of typed changes the user accepts in full or in part. Anchor previews check section
anchors against the dev samples.

tags.name: Test runs
tags.description: Test runs process samples with the open draft. They are never delivered to the target.

tags.name: Evaluation, iterations & comparisons
tags.description:
An evaluation runs the draft over a sample set and scores the outputs against the
references; each evaluation is recorded as an iteration with a snapshot of the definition.
Comparisons run several models over the same samples.

tags.name: Feedback & revise
tags.description:
Feedback notes on dev samples and iterations, and the **revise** stage, which proposes
changes from the open feedback and the latest evaluation failures.

tags.name: Holdout & publish gate
tags.description:
Holdout reference runs and the publish gate: a version is published only when its newest
holdout evaluation covers every ready holdout sample and scores at or above the project's
threshold, unless an override reason is given.

tags.name: Bundles
tags.description:
Export a project as a zip bundle (samples, prepared text, brief, draft and drafting
context) and import one as a new project.

tags.name: Auth & sessions
tags.description:
Sign in with an email address and a password to get a session cookie (`ih_session`).
Every `/api` route needs the session except sign-in, sign-out and these docs. See
[ADR 0013](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-email-password-users.md).

tags.name: Profile
tags.description:
Your own profile: name, job title, company and LinkedIn name, and a linked GitHub account
(its picture is your picture in the app) with the repository recipe YAML will be stored in.
The email address is changed by an admin.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
Admins add people with a name, an email address and a one-time password, and can edit,
disable, unlock or reissue them, and read recent sign-ins. The admin from the API log signs
in as `admin` with the token the API prints on every start.

tags.name: Data-lake S3 keys
tags.description:
Read-only S3 credentials for data-lake consumers of the publish bucket. Secrets are shown
once. See [ADR 0008](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-s3-read-keys.md).

tags.name: Ontologies
tags.description:
The ontology library: customer and industry ontologies (OWL/RDFS, SKOS, SHACL) that
document types map their outputs to. Admins import a file as a new immutable version;
the worker parses it and indexes its terms, which anyone signed in can browse. See
[ADR 0011](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-rdf-publishing-and-ontologies.md).

tags.name: Linked data
tags.description:
The deployment's customer and the base IRI its RDF is minted under (ADR 0011). One
customer per deployment; without their own base, IRIs live under
`https://id.stocks-hayward.com/<customer>/`.

tags.name: Published outputs
tags.description:
Publishing targets: the S3 buckets published outputs are delivered to. Each recipe names one
(`delivery.publishTo`, absent = `default`, seeded from `.env`); every delivered output
records its target, so it is read and withdrawn there whatever changes later. A target in
use keeps its bucket, prefix, endpoint and region.

tags.name: Bridge
tags.description:
The delivery bridge publishing goes through: a link to its connections page (where
credentials are kept, never in CT Studio), and the routes the bridge calls back, signed with
the shared `BRIDGE_CLIENT_KEY` rather than a session.

tags.name: GitHub
tags.description:
Syncing transformation recipes with a GitHub repository: this deployment's instance name
and default folder, a document type's repository link, and pushing a published version
as a YAML file with the signed-in user's own linked GitHub account. Admins set the
settings and links; anyone with a linked account can push.

tags.name: Backup
tags.description:
Encrypted backups of the whole stack (database, objects, triple store) that an admin makes,
downloads and restores from Administration > Backup, and the job queue's pause switch. A
backup opens only with the `LLM_SECRETS_KEY` it was made under.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness checks for load balancers and orchestrators. They need no session.
